summary:
Crucible 4.0's synthetic internet is 22 kernel modules in src/crucible/services/ (182 @endpoint tools). They share one event-sourced World: identity, ledger, permissions and knowledge. id, bank, mail, forum, search, docs, code, issues, cal, support, ads, market, cloud, biz, contracts, jobs, wf, caps, deal, gov, net and db (appdb) are all ordinary Modules. Handlers emit events, appliers mutate tables, and money moves only through bank.move.

The social layer is text only:
- forum: boards fixed at genesis, posts, replies, votes, follows, and one hot-score feed.
- mail: delayed delivery and bounces.
- docs: versioned public or private documents.
- search: BM25 multiplied by a pluggable rank_signal.
- ads: keyword bid campaigns shown as sponsored search results, charged per impression.

Software and hosting:
- code: content-addressed string blobs (64 KB per file, 2 MB per repo), linear history, a crucible.json deps list, code.run and code.test in the sandbox.
- cloud: providers, instances, `cloud.deploy` of a repo whose manifest declares endpoints and optionally a `web` section with routes and static files. Each deployment is a sandboxed service principal svc:<host>. Calls are metered in compute units against instance capacity, and the service can overload, suffer outages or be suspended for unpaid bills.
- net: one recorded `net.fetch` command per HTTP request. It also provides DNS names, sessions, consent login, rate limits and a daily crawler that indexes pages and builds a link-authority signal. appdb gives each app its own storage namespace.

Tool discovery:
- `World.available_tools` lists the built-in tools plus every host the principal has 'learned' (from search results, reads, `world.describe`).
- `world.find_tools`, `world.hosts`, `world.validate`, `world.help` and `world.api` support lookup and dry runs.
- MCP sends `tools/list_changed` when the list changes.
- `wf` flows and triggers compose tools; `caps.publish` and `caps.install` delegate scoped grants to a service.

Browser mode is a FastAPI and Jinja front end (web/app.py). GET pages go through `World.query`, which always rolls back; POST /_act calls `World.execute`. Playwright BrowserSession resolves only *.crucible and blocks all other requests. A test asserts that a browser session and the same headless calls produce bit-identical event logs.

Sandbox: boot.py drops to uid nobody, sets NO_NEW_PRIVS and applies Landlock ABI 4 (filesystem plus TCP). seccomp denies socket, exec, fork, ptrace, mount, bpf, io_uring and similar calls. runner.py sets rlimits (address space, CPU, process count, open files, file size, no core dumps), a wall-clock timeout per job, and JSON-lines RPC through `crucible_sdk.call`. Only numpy can be imported. Outcomes are recorded through ctx.reserve/fill so regeneration is exact.

Real-world access is OFF by default (modes.py and realworld/ bridge), and a red-team probe suite covers Gate-W-style attacks. There are no image, audio or video artifacts, no media tooling, no recommendation engines beyond the forum feed, search and ads, and simulated people do not browse web sites.

data_model_and_state:
All authoritative state lives in World.state tables, declared in Module.install with secondary indexes (`st.declare_table(name, index=(...))`). Tables change only through @applier functions run on events from ctx.emit(type, payload, vis). vis is 'public', 'internal', or a tuple of principals, and World.visible_events filters on it.

Ids:
- Ids come from st.new_id(prefix): fpost_*, freply_*, adc_*, inst_*, dep_*, mail_*, doc_*, proj_*, iss_*, tkt_*, flow_*, hw_*.
- Repo ids are '<handle>/<name>'. Blob ids are 'b'+blake2b(12). Commit ids are 'c'+blake2b(10) over [rid, parent, tree, msg, author, now].
- Principals: p:<handle> (person), o:<handle> (org), svc:<host> (deployed service, info {operator, host}), sys.

Key tables:
- forum: forum_boards, forum_posts, forum_replies, forum_votes ('<post>|<voter>'), forum_follows ('<follower>|<target>').
- search: search_docs.
- ads: ads_campaigns, ads_kw ('<kw>|<cid>').
- code: repos, commits, blobs ({content: str, size}), compute_use.
- cloud: providers, instances, hosts, deployments (with manifest, svc, trusted, cu_est, errors), svc_days, svc_hours.
- net: domains, web_sessions ('<host>|<visitor>'), web_pages, web_links, web_rate, web_days.
- appdb: app_docs ('<ns>|<coll>|<id>').
- knowledge: '<principal>|<kind>|<value>', which drives tool lists.

Runtime caches live in world.runtime (search.index, sandbox_pool, trusted_fns, cloud.running), are never persisted, and are dropped in on_load.

Nondeterministic external work (sandbox runs, trusted CPU timing) is recorded as ctx.ext outcomes (reserve/fill or external) in an 'ext' event. Regeneration returns the recorded outcome and re-issues the recorded brokered RPCs in order.

Persistence goes through Store (memory://, sqlite:///, postgresql://) with a hash chain over events and pickle snapshots. WorldServer persists per-actor cursors and tool lists under 'session/<wid>/<principal>', and SHA-256 token hashes under 'crucible-api/tokens/<world>'. Browser-mode sessions and SSO tickets are in memory only.
determinism_replay_persistence:
The kernel is single-threaded per world.

Each command is one transaction: on CrucibleError it rolls back and records cmd.rejected. Nested ctx.call uses savepoints.

Randomness comes only from ctx.rng(*keys), which is seeded by (spec.seed, 'cmd', seq, counter). Iteration is sorted everywhere, e.g. the BM25 scores accumulate in sorted term order with integer stats.

The search inverted index is a runtime cache reconciled against records by identity. check_invariants compares it with a from-scratch rebuild (search.py:330-343).

Sandbox outputs (stdout, cpu_ms, result, rpcs) are recorded. With params cost_model='deterministic', CPU is counted as executed Python lines (LINE_MS = 0.001 nominal ms per line), and import work is not counted, so cost is the same in fresh and warm workers. Tests: test_deterministic_cost_of_a_request_does_not_depend_on_whether_the_worker_is_fresh and test_a_fork_with_fresh_sandbox_workers_evolves_exactly_like_its_parent.

Browser equivalence: page GETs use World.query, which always rolls back. A form POST is exactly one World.execute. test_browser_workflow_equals_headless asserts an identical digest, seq and last_hash.

Emitted payloads must never be mutated afterwards (SECURITY.md:143-147).

Code blobs are stored in full inside internal 'code.blob' event payloads, so the event log grows with content size.
extension_points: New social platforms (video, images, newsletters, social graph, communities, messaging): a new `@register_module class X(Module)` with `host`, endpoints, appliers and processes (core/kernel.py:130-179). It registers by import in services/__init__.py:2-3, and its tools then appear automatically in World.available_tools, world.find_tools, world.hosts, MCP and the web `/_api` fallback.

Discoverable content: call `search.index(ctx, doc_id, kind, title, text, owner, ref, hosts)` (services/search.py:83) with new kinds such as 'video', 'image', 'article' or 'newsletter' (KIND_RE allows any [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,23}); extend the KINDS list (search.py:43) for its description.

Recommendation and ranking: chain `world.hooks['rank_signal']` as net.py:89-96 does, and add a feeds hook analogous to `world.hooks['sponsored']` (ads.py:55). gaps_vs_v5_spec.gap: Only text forum, mail, docs, search and ads exist. There is no short-form or long-form video, no images, no creator subscriptions, no newsletters, no social network beyond follow edges, no product-discovery platform separate from search and market, and no developer community or Q&A platform.

Everything is text.
- Code blobs are str with MAX_FILE 64 KiB and MAX_REPO 2 MiB (code.py:25-27).
- Web static files are limited to css/js/svg/txt/json (net.py:226-227).
- The browser front end drops multipart file uploads (web/app.py:2057), and templates have no img/audio/video.
- There are no sandboxed media tools. FFmpeg is installed at /usr/bin/ffmpeg but seccomp blocks execve, and only numpy is importable in the sandbox.
- There is no update/remove/analytics model for media artifacts.
No text, image, audio or video encoders and no embedding cache keyed by hash and encoder version. Search uses a lowercase regex tokenizer only.

Simulated people do not browse web sites (INTERNET_ARCHITECTURE.md:65). Consumers are a numpy population with small awareness sets. There is no per-participant attention or time budget for content consumption (the forum.feed limit is a per-call cap), and no return-to or leave-resource behaviour over pages or creators.

Only the forum hot-score feed, BM25 with rank_signal, and bid-ordered sponsored ads exist. Missing: collaborative filtering, learned engagement prediction, exploration, diversity-aware ranking, per-platform algorithms, algorithm change during a run, finite exposure allocation across competing content, delayed and noisy analytics, and evaluator-hidden algorithm parameters.

No impressions, unique exposed identities, views, watch duration, completion, shares or returning-viewer counters for content. Forum posts carry only votes and replies. Ads count charged impressions. net counts hits per day by outcome. No compact-ID or estimated-population mode.

Boards are created only at genesis from config['boards'] (forum.py:60-64), and create_board is internal with no endpoint, so participants cannot form communities. Boards have no membership, roles, moderation, governance, trust, entry/exit or inactivity tracking. The gov module applies to organisations, not forum communities. Delete is author-only, with no reports or moderation queue.

No pull requests or merge requests, no independent code review, no releases, tags or semver, no package registry or package search beyond kind 'repo' in search, no compatibility checking, and no branches (history is linear). Dependency incorporation (crucible.json deps <= 10, code.py:82) is not tracked as adoption evidence outside caps.

Observation has no artifact references, semantic representations or resource-usage fields. observe() has no explicit cursor argument (the cursor is server-side), though replay_events(from_seq, actor) covers observe_since. Missing or uncertain information and delayed-consequence provenance are not typed.
Mostly present. Missing: generic file creation outside repos (no per-agent workspace), media content-creation tools, and wrapped screenshot or visual observation in BrowserSession.

There is no legacy_shaped_reward / verified_terminal_outcome / observation_only mode switch. CrucibleEnv reward is objective.step_reward (gym_env.py:164-167), and the CAM2 adapter uses potential shaping.

The CAM2 and SL adapters import agentrs.cam2 / agentrs.sl at module top. They fail to import without ../src on sys.path (find_spec('agentrs') is False in the default env), so an architecture-independent reference learner suite is needed for acceptance.

The sandbox is process-level only (no VM, gVisor or bubblewrap on this host). The social layer has no participant consent, abuse reporting, moderation or anti-fabricated-engagement mechanisms, and there is no login rate limiting in browser mode. The new audience metrics will need protection against direct writes, which is only proven today for ads, votes and revenue.

Sandbox, evaluator isolation, reward hacking, accounting, resource limits, network and private-state tests exist. Missing: an explicit cross-world contamination test (fork isolation exists in test_api, and sandbox pool keys include world_id), audience-metric manipulation probes (sockpuppet views or follows, self-shares), and media-processing resource-exhaustion tests.

Gate J holds for API-service products used by consumers and for capabilities installed by NPC firms. Web-app products are used only by agents and the crawler, not by the population. No content, media or educational-product category is consumed by the population.

risks_and_gotchas: SandboxConfig has no `backend` or `min_isolation` fields (runner.py:44-60; confirmed via dataclasses.fields). runner.py:204-206 reads them with getattr, falling back to env CRUCIBLE_SANDBOX_BACKEND / CRUCIBLE_MIN_ISOLATION. SECURITY.md:136 says `SandboxConfig.min_isolation`, but SandboxConfig(min_isolation=...) would raise TypeError.

seccomp denies execve, fork and vfork (boot.py:101, 139), and APPROVED_PACKAGES is ('numpy',) (runner.py:39); test_isolation_matrix asserts torch import is blocked. Neither FFmpeg (a binary) nor Pillow/torchvision can run inside the current sandbox, so media tooling needs a new sandbox profile or a broker-side recorded tool.

Code blob contents are carried in full in internal `code.blob` event payloads (code.py:124). Putting media in events would make logs, snapshots and replay grow without bound. A content-addressed store outside the log, with hashes in events, is needed and must be included in snapshot, fork and replay integrity.

The sandbox pool config is read once from world params and cached in world.runtime['sandbox_pool'] (code.py:167-182). All workers share uid nobody, so RLIMIT_NPROC=512 is a total across workers. Container pids.max is 2816 per memory notes, and each Chromium is about 80 threads (SCALING.md:71); at most about 2 concurrent BrowserSessions are safe.

BrowserSession has no screenshot method, although INTERNET_ARCHITECTURE.md:20 claims screenshots are available. Only the raw Playwright `page` attribute could take one. Not confirmed as a wrapped API.

Page views through World.query never record learn() or ad-impression side effects (SYNTHETIC_INTERNET.md:429-433). Any v5 'view' counted from browser page renders would be lost, so a consumption event must be a recorded command.
Agent web apps get CSP `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` (web/app.py:821-825), but built-in pages are script-free (app.py:1012). Agent JS runs in Chromium, though only *.crucible is reachable.

Search check_invariants rebuilds the whole index from scratch (search.py:340-342). ads.seen_today scans the ledger per viewer on every search (ads.py:159-171). forum.feed scans the last 50 posts per followed source (forum.py:257-262). None of these scale to millions of artifacts or viewers.
Deployed-service endpoints have fixed cost_s=5 (cloud.py:86), and a service cannot call itself in one call chain (cloud.py:200-206).

Trusted in-process exec of genesis code (cloud.py:242-255) depends on provenance. Any commit through the public tools permanently untrusts a repo (code.py:95-98, 384). New world generators that ship code must preserve this.

The real-world bridge must never be imported by world code (red-team probe independence.world_code_cannot_import_evaluator_or_bridge). New media or encoder modules must not import crucible.realworld or evaluation internals.
Payload immutability: emitted event payloads must never be mutated afterwards. The kernel does not copy them (SECURITY.md:143-147).
Browser-mode sessions, SSO tickets and the mail cache are in memory only (SYNTHETIC_INTERNET.md:456-457). There is no login rate limiting.
The CAM2/SL integration modules import agentrs at top level, and agentrs is not importable from the default Python path here (importlib find_spec returned False).
